title.narrative: Life-saving multi-sectoral humanitarian assistance to address the most critical needs of internally displaced people in Mekelle IDP Camps, Tigray Regional State

description.narrative: ltpgtThe rapid assessments carried out by the LWF teams in the Tigray region (see attached document) reveal that IDPs in Mekelle are experiencing serious difficulties in fulfilling their basic needs, accessing services, and securing livelihoods that support their living conditions. These challenges include insufficient water supply and access to WASH NFIs, protection risks—especially for women and girls—and shelter and NFI-related issues among IDPs residing in camps and collection centers of Mekelle city of Tigray.ltbrgtThe proposed project aims to address the multifaceted humanitarian needs of internally displaced populations (IDPs) in Mekelle city of Tigray region, targeting 74,580 individuals (38,791 women and 35,789 men). It seeks to improve living conditions and uphold the dignity of IDPs through the provision and enhancement of WASH services, multipurpose cash assistance, camp coordination and camp management (CCCM), shelter and NFI support, and protection interventions. This integrated approach will improve access to essential services, reduce protection risks, and support vulnerable households in meeting their immediate and recovery needs.ltbrgtCurrently, LWF is implementing various development and humanitarian projects across Tigray, with its coordination office in Mekelle city. The proposed projects focus on Protection, CCCM, MPC, ES NFIs, and WASH, benefiting both IDPs and host communities in locations of Sebacare and Mai Woyini.ltbrgtIn response to the urgent humanitarian needs, LWF and its national partner—MAEDOTAID—plan to collaborate on a comprehensive response covering protection, WASH, multi-purpose cash, CCCM and ES NFIs. Although the partner is currently not implementing partner under EHF/OCHA, it possess extensive experience in health, protection, MHPSS and nutrition, working closely with displaced populations. MAEDOTAID works in Tigray, responding to IDPs in Adigrat and Mekelle IDP camps with a focus on health, GBV, protection, nutrition, and MHPSS. Additionally, LWF plans to build the capacity of the national NGO to improve its ability to manage humanitarian responses effectively and access institutional funding, such as the CBPF. ltbrgtWASH interventions will focus on provision of WASH Kits and improved hygiene and sanitation practices in targeted IDP camps. Protection and GBV interventions aim to deliver essential, life-saving assistance to survivors and individuals at increased protection risks including gender-based violence. Through community-based protection as well as survivor-centered approaches, the proposed project seeks to enhance protection, restore dignity, and boost the resilience of the most vulnerable IDPs.ltbrgtThe project will also support vulnerable IDP households in accessing services and fulfilling basic needs through multipurpose cash transfers. These services will adhere to international humanitarian standards and protection principles. Rather than a blanket approach, the ES NFI assistance will target only those households most in need of immediate shelter NFIs. The CCCM interventions will focus on maintenance of communal facilities and enhanced local governance of targeted camps. ltbrgtAcross all sectors, protection, gender, and disability considerations are embedded in line with the EHF Directive on Cross-Cutting Issues. By adopting a holistic, rights-based approach, the proposed project aims to address both the immediate humanitarian needs of IDPs and their recovery efforts.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
